purpose: Bind connectivity evidence to a versioned software/radio/carrier-settings snapshot so results are not generalized from model name alone.

dimensions.purpose: Non-secret device identity needed to compare software snapshots.
User-visible OS release and API generation.
Build-level identity kept distinct from user-visible OS version.
dimensions.boundary: Android Build.FINGERPRINT uniquely identifies a build but must not be parsed for inferred semantics.

dimensions.purpose: Security and modular update state that may change without changing the marketing OS name.
Baseband/modem/radio firmware state separate from OS/build.
dimensions.boundary: A published suffix or partial value never reconstructs a full modem/baseband version.

dimensions.purpose: OEM UI/version channel and vendor software identifiers.
Carrier-side device configuration version where the platform exposes it.
dimensions.boundary: A newer carrier-settings version does not automatically mean better compatibility.

dimensions.purpose: Where and when the snapshot was observed or published.
Link connectivity results to the exact or partial software snapshot that produced them.

notes: Build.FINGERPRINT uniquely identifies the build and should not be parsed.
Build.getRadioVersion() returns the radio firmware version and can return null.
SECURITY_PATCH is the user-visible date of the most recently applied security patch.
INCREMENTAL represents the underlying source-control build value.
System, modular system components, and kernel can have separate effective patch/version states.
Apple exposes modem firmware and carrier/network information in About.
Carrier Settings Version can change independently of the iOS marketing version.
Apple documents that system files can be updated without changing the software version.
Some Samsung Japan tables publish only the last three characters of the baseband version; store them as a suffix, not a full value.

non_inference_rules: Same model name does not imply the same software snapshot.
Same Android/iOS marketing version does not imply the same build, baseband/modem firmware or carrier settings.
Same One UI version does not imply the same baseband.
Same baseband suffix does not prove the same full baseband string.
Published latest-version data does not prove a user's device has installed that version.
A connectivity result is exact only when the tested software snapshot is explicitly observed.
A carrier operation-check result must not be bound to the manufacturer's latest baseband unless that exact baseband/build was part of the test evidence.
Carrier Settings Version and modem firmware are independent fields.
Android security patch, Google Play system update, system modules and kernel state may differ within the same OS generation.
Software updates can improve or regress behavior; newer is not automatically better for every connectivity function.
Runtime evidence remains valid only for its recorded conditions unless a wider scope is separately demonstrated.
Do not infer CSC/regional channel from unofficial code lists.
